chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who struck his daughter while she was pregnant, so she miscarried a dead foetus. The husband of the woman complained against him. The woman said to her husband, 'If there is a wergild (blood money) for this foetus, and I have inheritance rights in it, then my inheritance from it is for my father.' He said: 'It is permissible for her father whatever she gifts him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father inheriting from his daughter's share of a miscarried foetus?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the financial rights associated with a miscarried foetus, specifically addressing the scenario where the father strikes his pregnant daughter. The Imam rules that the daughter may gift her share of the foetus's inheritance to her father, and he accepts it, highlighting the flexibility of inheritance distribution among close relatives in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the concept of 'diyah' (blood money) for the foetus and the legal capacity of the mother to dispose of her inherited share before the foetus is fully born or its status is finalized.
